items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Well, I played with Thomas a while. Yeah, I played with Thomas two or three times. I went with his band and left him.

ctx.x: No. Now was he the leader of the band? Yeah. This Edwauke Clem? Yeah. He was the leader of the band. What kind of style did he play? Can you think of anybody that we heard that he played like? Let's see who. I don't remember now. Well like Kid Thomas?

Well partly like Thomas. Yeah partly like Thomas. How about Charlie Love? But he had a, a, a tongue in his thing. You know like cutting over. Uh huh. See a, see a cutting over the tongue like that. Did he play anything like Charlie Love? No. I think it's more like Thomas.
Did he have any feature number?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: Yeah I played pretty good with Thomas in the early days.

ctx.x: I just wonder, was it before World War I or... Um... Oh yeah, that's before World War I. It was coming. What was his right name?

Who is it? You don't know? I just don't know. And Tano says that you asked me about none of the musicians' right name. To tell the truth about it. That's the point you said. Well you're the only one who knows Ambrose's name, man. I never got that. Well some only know a name. All right, you take, for instance, you take Howard. I just got Howard's name. This was about two years ago, as long as I've been knowing him. And when he started with us in Kelly's band, he was a drummer. And I just know him lately here.…
No way. Never goes into that. Well let me ask you something. When you wanted to get in touch with these fellas for jobs, how did you find them if you didn't know their right names?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Cag; Cag is only mentioned by the interviewer in the context of seeing 'Cag and Paul Barnes' at a club.

ctx.x: It's fun. I don't believe they had a crowd, though.

I don't know. I don't know, I saw Cag and Paul Barnes there, he wasn't doing badly. No. Well, that was the job that you fixed up for Paul, I guess. You must have called you when you sent Paul, huh? Yeah. Well, you worked at any of these other little clubs, did you, really?
Like, other neighborhood places? I worked at the River Bell, out here on, on, on, Crue and Chord, I believe, on that side of the band. That was before you went to the Hominé Inn? No after.
